title: Topic 4 – Accounting for financial debt and equity
source: Zusammenfassung von „IFRS Topic 4 Fall 2026 student version“ (+ Anleihen aus den Klausuren)

blocks.text: Relevant standards: IAS 32 (presentation – debt or equity), IFRS 9 (recognition and measurement), IFRS 7 (disclosures), IFRS 13 (fair value), IFRS 2 (share-based payment). The issuer classifies under IAS 32 and measures liabilities under IFRS 9; the holder uses the same classification to choose its IFRS 9 category.
Debt or equity? The criterion is a contractual obligation of the issuer to transfer financial assets:
children: Obligation to pay ongoing compensation ('interest') and/or to repay at maturity → financial liability
Instruments puttable by the holder → liability
Probability of payment is irrelevant; conditions outside the issuer's control are irrelevant
The name of the instrument and of the payments is irrelevant

blocks.text: The classification also drives the treatment of compensation (interest = expense, dividends = distribution) and of issue costs (equity: deducted from equity; debt: included in the effective interest).
Hybrid instruments (subordinated, perpetual, deferrable interest) are classified by the same criterion – often equity, while cheaper than ordinary shares.

Compound instruments (convertible bonds, bonds with warrants) are split at issuance: liability component first (PV at market rate), equity component as the remainder. There is no intermediate category between liabilities and equity under IFRS.

children: Share capital at par, the excess in share premium; issue costs reduce share premium
Treasury shares are deducted from equity at cost; resale or cancellation never creates a gain or loss in P/L
Reasons for buy-backs: distribute cash, increase EPS/ROE, employee plans, acquisitions, takeover defence, market making

blocks.text: Bonds measured at amortised cost (exam topic): initial amount = issue price; interest expense = effective rate × opening carrying amount; cash paid = coupon; the difference amortises the discount until nominal value is reached.
A contractual obligation to deliver cash or another financial asset (IAS 32).
A contract that evidences a residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting all of its liabilities.
An instrument containing both a liability and an equity component, e.g. a convertible bond.
An entity's own shares that it has reacquired; deducted from equity.
The rate that exactly discounts the estimated future cash payments to the initial carrying amount of the financial liability.
